subject: Sprint‑Zero: Pilot charter, success metrics & access agreement
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Romero <alicia@novushealth.io>, David Chen <dchen@novushealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint‑Zero: Pilot charter, success metrics & access agreement

Hi Alicia + David — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations before we kick off the pilot (Sprint‑Zero).

Pain points you articulated
- High latency on inference for batch post‑processing (especially peak daytime traffic)
- Cost unpredictability when models scale during load spikes
- Need for strict data isolation and audit logs for PHI flows

Pilot goals (agreed)
1) Reduce 95th‑percentile inference latency to < 300ms for the 1–2k token range for the targeted endpoint
2) Demonstrate 30% cost reduction per 1k requests using prefix/KV caching and batching compared to current baseline
3) Verify audit logging and KMS integration meet your compliance checklist for a subset of traffic

Scope for Sprint‑Zero (2 weeks) — what we propose
- Baseline measurement (we collect 48 hours of traces / sample corpus)
- Deploy a scoped Redwood Dedicated testing pool with the model you requested (quantized variant)
- Run 3 eval prompt sets (latency, hallucination check, and regression set)
- Provide a one‑page runbook and access checklist for your infra team

Owners / point people
- Novus Health: Alicia Romero (product), David Chen (infra)
- Redwood: Naomi Feldman (Engagement lead), Ben Carter (SE lead), Priyom Das (Onboarding / support)

Immediate asks from Novus (please confirm by EOD):
- Confirm the sample dataset location (S3 path or staged drive) and at least one representative prompt set
- Provide an initial list of IP ranges for access and a sandbox service account for onboarding (minimal IAM scope)

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft pilot charter and an access checklist we can iterate on. I’ll follow up with a shared Drive folder and a DocuSign envelope for the SOW once you confirm scope.

Next steps
- You: confirm dataset location and service account by 06/04
- Us: unblock infra and share access steps, schedule a 1‑hour kickoff session (tech deep dive) for next week

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555‑0123

Attachments: NHI-pilot-charter-v1.pdf (12KB), NHI-access-instructions.md (4KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Romero <alicia@novushealth.io>, David Chen <dchen@novushealth.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint‑Zero: Pilot charter, success metrics & access agreement

Quick technical notes — adding these to the charter draft so infra has clarity: 

- For latency testing we’ll want a representative distribution of sequence lengths (short: 50–150 tokens, medium: 300–800 tokens, long: 1k–2k). If you can flag typical endpoints or traffic slices, we’ll create matching synthetic traffic.
- Regarding the quantized model variant: we recommend trying the 4‑bit quantized build if you need the cost/throughput gains; we’ll hold a canary on a small pool first.
- Network: for private deployment please provide the sandbox VPC peering details and the NHI NAT gateway egress ranges. If you prefer, we can use a lightweight connector and leave model execution in Redwood Dedicated for Sprint‑Zero to speed onboarding.

I’ll be on the kickoff call — happy to walk through the runbook and the KV cache setup (simple changes to your inference client).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: 2026-06-03T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint‑Zero: Pilot charter, success metrics & access agreement

Thanks Naomi — this summary captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: we’ll stage a ~10k sample payload in S3 under s3://novus-prod-sandbox/pilot/samples by COB 06/04. Will that size be sufficient for baseline runs?
2) Service account: we can open a sandbox role with S3 read only + temporary secrets access; David — I’ll loop you to provide the exact principal.
3) Compliance: we need to validate the audit log retention period — our compliance team requires logs for 6 months. Can Redwood provide export/retention options?

Also, can you itemize the minimal ports and IP ranges needed to allow the connector? We prefer the connector path to avoid inbound firewall exceptions if possible.

We’ll confirm the kickoff time after David checks calendar availability.

Thanks,
Alicia Romero
Director, Product Operations
Novus Health
aliciasig@novushealth.io

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Romero <alicia@novushealth.io>, David Chen <dchen@novushealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint‑Zero kickoff materials — charter + access checklist (attached)

Alicia / David — per our asks below I’ve attached an updated pilot charter (v1) and a short access checklist. Highlights and changes: 

- Baseline size: 10k sample set is fine for the initial latency and regression checks; we recommend a follow‑on 48–72 hour capture for production‑like traffic once the integration is stable.
- Audit logs: Redwood can retain logs for 6 months in our hosted retention tier; we’ll include an export job to push a copy to your S3 bucket daily. Please sign the attached SSA (DocuSign link in the Drive) to enable PHI pathways.
- Network connector: we’ll default to an outbound connector approach (no inbound firewall openings). Minimal egress: allow outbound to 52.23.45.0/24 and 34.198.12.0/24 on ports 443 and 2200 (for agent mgmt). If you want to avoid the agent, we can do an S3 replication + transient presigned URLs approach.

Attached: NHI-pilot-charter-v1.pdf (charter + success metrics), NHI-access-instructions.md (step‑by‑step for service account + connector), network-diagram.png (high level).

Proposed immediate schedule:
- 06/04: Novus confirms S3 path + service account
- 06/07: 60‑minute kickoff call (tech deep dive) — propose 10:00 PT; Redwood will share an agenda
- 06/08–06/18: Sprint‑Zero execution window (measure, deploy canary, run evals)

Please review the charter and sign the SSA when ready. I’ve also uploaded the folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cNovusPilot

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: NHI-pilot-charter-v1.pdf, NHI-access-instructions.md, network-diagram.png

Date: 2026-06-06T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint‑Zero kickoff materials — charter + access checklist (attached)

Thanks Naomi — all looks good. Quick confirmations from infra: 

- We’ve staged the samples at s3://novus-prod-sandbox/pilot/samples and created the sandbox role (principal: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/novus-pilot‑sandbox). I’ll send the role ARN and a temporary key via the secure channel you mentioned.
- IP ranges: we can open outbound to the two CIDR blocks you provided for the connector. If the agent needs additional control plane ports we’ll temporarily allow 2201 as well.
- Audit export: confirm you will deliver a daily export to s3://novus-prod-sandbox/pilot/logs with 6‑month retention. We’ll need the config for the lifecycle rules on our side.

I’m good for the kickoff on 06/07 at 10:00 PT — Alicia will send the calendar invite. Can you share a short agenda and the tech deep‑dive owners?

—David Chen
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Novus Health
dchen@novushealth.io
